newTheorem.statement: For the two-parameter zero-sum family [a,-b,c,b-c-a] on a fixed finite integer domain X, every forbidden support occurs on an integer parameter line b(x4-x2)+c(x3-x4)=a(x4-x1). Therefore the full (b,c)-plane is partitioned exactly by finitely many tuple-lines into support-hypergraph chambers; points off their union have the empty hypergraph.
newTheorem.proof: Expand the relation and collect b and c. Every ordered distinct tuple contributes exactly one linear Diophantine condition, and conversely every parameter point on that line realizes that tuple. Canonicalizing tuple supports and hashing their incident lines gives exact chamber equality.

exactRejectionBoundary.exactBoundary: For fixed X, parameters outside the finite union of emitted tuple-lines have no forbidden support. Equal optima do not imply equal chambers.

compressedExplanation: The one-parameter ratio cells become a two-dimensional line arrangement. A tuple is not guessed by search: it writes the exact line on which it exists. Chamber hashes then make parameter equivalence mechanical.
